deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is the outer address leaf of a folded letter, reused as scrap paper. It carries two red wax seals (top right and bottom right) and the archival foliation '10'.

In ink, in a formal hand, is the address: 'An den Kirchenvorstand / ad manus des Herrn Pa[stor ...]', i.e. a letter to a church council, to be delivered into the hands of the pastor. The text is cut off at the right edge by the fold.

Below it, in pencil and in a different, cursive hand, is a list of German adjectives in -ig/-lich. Some are followed by question marks and one is struck through. They look like word-formation or vocabulary jottings, possibly about adjectives derived from verbs or nouns. Examples are 'gefällig', 'zweideutig', 'gehörig', 'eigenartig(?)', 'abhängig', 'auffällig', 'eingängig?' and 'stutzig'. One gloss in parentheses links a noun to a phrase ('(Geschwätz?: schiefes Maul)'). There is also a quoted phrase with 'stößig ... stoßen'.

Nothing connects this to the surrounding mathematical material:
- The previous page derives the coefficients p = -(α+β-(α'+β')x)/(1-x) and q = (αβ-α'β'x)/(1-x) of the second-order ODE for Riemann's P-function.
- The next page bears the heading 'Zur Theorie der Gauss'schen Function F(α,β,γ,x)' and the note 'Erbschaft von Justus William Ebell'.

The sheet is evidently a recycled letter wrapper in the bundle. The pencil notes are linguistic, not mathematical, and may not be in Riemann's hand.

results.what: Address leaf of a letter to a church council (Kirchenvorstand, care of the pastor) plus pencil list of German adjectives; no mathematical content

deep.surprise_reason: The page has no mathematical content. It is a reused letter cover with an address and a pencil word list. It is of minor biographical or provenance interest only, possibly related to Riemann's family connections to the church (his father was a pastor).
transcription_corrections: The ink address reads 'An / den Kirchenvorstand / ad manus des Herrn Pa[stor?]'; the final word is truncated at the fold, so 'Pa[?]' is better given as probably 'Pastor'.

The pencil notes are in a different hand and medium (pencil) from the ink address. Readings of individual adjectives (e.g. 'absonderlich', 'abwegig', 'schwermüthig', 'geschwätzig', 'eigenartig', 'zuverlässig') are highly uncertain. Several could be other -ig words (e.g. 'schwerfällig' instead of 'schwermüthig').
The line rendered 'Zeit[?] .. [?]' is illegible and should be marked as such rather than given a reading.
The struck-through last word is uncertain ('eintönig' or similar); it repeats the first word of the list, which is followed by a question mark.
The page has two wax seals and the archival folio number '10' (top right), which the transcription does not mention.
